descriptions.text: Scroll of Meat Hooks. Let's be real. Every pet owner already has this spell, at least when it comes to their own pets. Sometimes it's the sound of a can opener. Or a command, such as "chow time, Fido!" Sometimes it's the wisp of a jar of peanut butter being cracked open. No matter what the trigger is, the effect is the same. You do something, and your pets come running. Meat Hooks works on the same principle. You cast, and pets come to you. …

beats.headline: Off a dead city elf
beats.text: Vicente the city elf has almost 1,500 gold in his inventory and one other item, a scroll, which Donut takes. It is for a spell called Meat Hooks, the one he had been casting when Mongo rushed into the alley: it summons all nearby carnivorous pet-class monsters away from their owners to the source of a burning stench. I knew he was a good boy, says Donut. He'd been summoned, and he couldn't help it. Carl tells her to hold onto it. You never know when it might be useful.

beats.headline: Read from a plane
beats.text: Orthrus, an enormous two-headed puppy, has to be got out of the water and out of his bubble, and Donut still has the scroll from the third floor. Carl rereads it first: thirty seconds plus ten per point of the caster's intelligence, a hundred metres plus twenty per point of charisma. With Donut's numbers that is just over nine minutes and almost three kilometres. Read the scroll, he calls from the plane, and the stench trails behind them like a blown engine. Donut is going to vomit. The puppy pulls itself off the necropolis, tips over the edge of the bubble and tumbles out. Quest complete.

beats.headline: Still spewing
beats.text: Orthrus whimpers below. Donut heals him back up to seventy percent, and the renewed health renews the dog's interest in chasing them at once. The Meat Hooks spell is still spewing from Donut's paw. Carl turns the plane sharply between two bubbles, growing more confident at the controls, and then a metal-skinned dirigible shaped like a fish comes out of nowhere in front of them, full of more crawlers.
